correctness.rationale: The exact Q(sqrt(5)) program generates exactly 30 midpoint vertices, enumerates every 27,405 four-subset, agrees between two determinant expansions for each and checks exact order of 27 values. The maximum 60 vertex sets, the 240 second-level sets and twenty facial families follow from exhaustive replacement tests. The multilinear convex-combination argument proves the continuous global maximum and uniqueness of the single moving vertex; 120 exact symmetry permutations certify the single 60-member orbit. Finite exhaustion is complete for this explicitly bounded object, not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: Maximum-volume tetrahedra in a highly symmetric 30-vertex Archimedean solid form a natural extremal geometry problem. The result classifies all continuous equality cases into 20 two-dimensional facial families, identifies the unique long-side anchor triangle opposite each moving face, and gives the sharp discrete volume gap and multiplicity; these are not routine consequences of the known total body volume or vertex list. The new facts have direct meaning for inscribed-simplex optimization and symmetry reduction.
